name: John Sweeney

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Sweeney is a retired Portland Parks & Recreation supervisor.
bio.excerpt: John Sweeney is a retired Portland Parks & Recreation supervisor.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Mercury (Mercury Election Strike Force, 2026-09-09), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

bio.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Sweeney is a retired captain in the Oregon Army National Guard.
bio.excerpt: He’s also a retired captain in the Oregon Army National Guard.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Mercury (Mercury Election Strike Force, 2026-09-09), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

positions.statement: OPB describes Sweeney as a mechanical designer who wants the city to deliver better on its taxes.
positions.excerpt: John Sweeney is a mechanical designer who wants the city to deliver better on its taxes

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in OPB (Alex Zielinski, 2026-10-07), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked. OPB calls Sweeney a mechanical designer, while the Mercury (b1) calls him a retired Parks supervisor. Each item attributes its claim to its outlet.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Sweeney lists saving city services by lowering taxes in downtown Portland as a priority.
positions.excerpt: Saving city services by lowering taxes in downtown Portland.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Tribune (Hannah Seibold, 2026-10-13), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Sweeney calls for shifting the homeless services system to Multnomah County.
positions.excerpt: shifting the homeless/houseless system to Multnomah County as per Resolution “A”.

verification.note: Excerpt confirmed verbatim in Portland Tribune (Hannah Seibold, 2026-10-13), re-fetched 2026-10-14. Attribution, tier, paraphrase and neutrality checked.

gaps: Voters' pamphlet statement not readable: the individual statement PDF in the county's Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide is a scan with no machine-readable text, and the full and large-print county pamphlet PDFs are cut off by the fetch tool (~105k characters) before the City of Portland section (pp. M-52 to M-66)
City filing form (AUD-120): amended version has no readable text; original is handwritten with no readable fields
No campaign website found in the pamphlet statement or filing form
No voting record (has not held elected office)

verification_summary.balance_notes: Race portland-council-d3 (21 candidates). Every candidate was searched in the same shared sources: the Mercury (2026-09-09), OPB (2026-10-07), the Tribune Q&A (2026-10-13), the Multnomah pamphlet and the 2026 AUD-120 forms. The pamphlet index lists a statement for this candidate, but the collector could not read it. The pamphlet PDF text is 104,260 characters and ends before the Portland section (M-53 to M-60), and the individual statement scan is not linked from the MOO guide page and could not be re-fetched. This is a source-access gap, confirmed. Both AUD-120 filings are unreadable (the amended one has no text; the original is a handwritten scan). Sweeney has 2 bio and 3 position items, all T3. The website gap's wording ('not in the pamphlet statement') is unconfirmable because the statement is unreadable. Older dated 2024 OPB and KATU profiles exist but were not used; the collector excluded 2024 sources consistently across the race. Incumbent=false confirmed (portland.gov/council).
